title: Quarterly roadmap orchestration for Private/VPC/on-prem (Roadmap Symphony)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a coordinated quarterly roadmap and activation calendar for Private (VPC/on-prem) features that aligns OKRs, engineering capacity, and customer activation windows. This ticket defines the orchestration plan (the 'Roadmap Symphony') to sequence feature deliveries, acceptance gates, rollout cohorts and fallbacks so Sales, Solutions, and Support can run predictable customer activations.

Scope: planning and runbook for Q2 deliveries only: - RBAC + enterprise KMS onboarding flows - Private control plane upgrade tooling and compatibility checks - Dedicated capacity activation API + billing signal integration - On-prem packaging & offline installer baseline - Console workflows for tenant rollouts (visibility, tracing, rollback)

Success criteria: - Roadmap publication with committed milestones and owners by 2026-02-28. - Clear activation calendar with at least three customer cohorts and assigned Solutions leads. - Engineering has identified critical dependencies and slotted them into sprints (ENG owners signoff). - Risk register with mitigations and go/no-go gates. - A/B rollout plan and canary criteria documented, including metrics to monitor (see outcome_metrics).

Stakeholders: Product (Aisha Patel, Marcus Chen), Engineering leads (Maria Gonzales, Jae Park), Design (Elena Ruiz), Solutions Eng (Samir Kapoor), Security & Compliance (Priya Desai), Sales GTM (Lindsey Carter).

Key deliverables: - Roadmap timeline PDF and Confluence page for Q2 activation roadmap (link below). - Sprint-level commitment map with engineering owners and required tickets. - Customer cohort activation calendar (dates + exporters). - Observability runbook and dashboards for rollout metrics. - Post-activation checklist and incident escalation paths.

Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PRD-Private-Q2-Roadmap-Symphony ; Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/Private-Q2-Roadmap ; GitHub kickoff epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-epic/pulls/42

Constraints & trade-offs: - We must balance early availability for high-value customers against system stability; recommended approach is to prioritize RBAC and KMS readiness for first cohort and defer nonessential console UX polish to later cohorts. - On-prem packaging increases QA overhead; propose a thin first-cut offline installer + hardening in Q3.

Rollout plan (high level): Cohort A (pilot customers, Feb-Apr) -> Cohort B (selected enterprise customers, May-Jun) -> Cohort C (broader ramp, July). Each cohort has an A/B canary with a 72-hour health window.

Acceptance_criteria: "Roadmap page published with milestones, owners, and dependency list; sprint commitments from ENG leads documented; activation calendar with named cohorts and Solutions leads; observability dashboard templates available for rollout; security review completed and signed off."
outcome_metrics: Activation velocity (number of tenants onboarded per month), Mean time to activate (MTTA) per tenant, Post-activation incident rate (P0/P1 per 100 tenants), Lead time to rollback, Customer satisfaction NPS for pilot cohort.
acceptance_criteria: Roadmap page published with milestones, owners, and dependency list; sprint commitments from ENG leads documented; activation calendar with named cohorts and Solutions leads; observability dashboard templates available for rollout; security review completed and signed off.
